messages:
Nora B.: Heads up  BrightNorth LLC charged NY sales tax on invoice BN-2026-11 even though we uploaded a resale certificate last month. Invoice total $4,320 with $324 tax. Should we ask for a credit note or provide additional docs?

Jamal K.: Can you paste the vendor portal timestamp where we uploaded the certificate? Need to confirm it was the correct ST-120 form and that it was accepted by their system.

Nora B.: I checked: our vendor portal shows a file named 'Redwood_ST120_signed.pdf' uploaded 2026-10-04 16:11 EDT and status = "pending review" (it never moved to active).

Sophie L.: If vendor never activated it, they'd still charge tax. Standard approach: request a tax credit/credit note for the tax amount and ask them to reissue a tax-exempt invoice, then we process a refund. We should also ask them why certificate wasn't accepted.

Tax-bot: Quick tax note: NY resale certificate = Form ST-120. For NY, reseller certificates must include buyer name, address, description of property, and signature. Digital copies are acceptable but vendor must retain it. If vendor charged tax incorrectly, the remedy is vendor-issued credit and corrected invoice. Buyer-provided certificate does not obligate vendor to retroactively remove tax unless vendor accepts it.

Jamal K.: OK place payment for invoice BN-2026-11 on hold for the tax amount portion. We'll pay principal once vendor issues corrected doc? Any risk if we don't hold full payment?

AP-bot: Payment hold set on BN-2026-11  reason: tax dispute (sales tax charged despite resale certificate). Hold applied to tax line only. AP queue notified.

Nora B.: Drafting vendor message. Sophie, can you review? Here's my draft: 

"Hi BrightNorth team, thanks for BN-2026-11. Our records show we uploaded a signed New York resale certificate (ST-120) on 2026-10-04. Your portal indicates the file remained in 'pending review' and we were still charged NY sales tax. To proceed please either: (A) issue a credit note for the sales tax amount ($324) and reissue an invoice without NY sales tax, or (B) confirm acceptance of our ST-120 and provide documentation showing when it was registered on your side. Payment of the tax portion will be held until resolved. Please respond within 5 business days. Regards, Nora on behalf of Redwood AP"

Sophie L.: Looks good. Add a line asking them to confirm the ship-to / billing address used to calculate tax (common source of mismatch). Also ask them to attach the portal screenshot showing acceptance if they claim it was accepted.

Nora B.: Updated message and sent to vendor at 2026-11-12T11:03:22Z cc: vendor-ops.

Tax-bot: Add-on: if vendor refuses to issue credit, we can file for a refund through vendor's state filing only if vendor agrees; otherwise we may pursue vendor for correction. Keep documentation: our uploaded ST-120, vendor portal screenshots, and the outbound message.

Jamal K.: Noted. I've added an internal note on the vendor record: "Resale certificate uploaded pending review 2026-10-04; vendor charged NY sales tax on BN-2026-11; awaiting credit note."

Nora B.: Closing loop for now. Reopen when vendor responds or if AP needs escalation. :white_check_mark:
